title: Prosecutor Investigating U.S. Boat Strikes and Claims of Torture Was Murdered in Ecuador
excerpt: New evidence has emerged of U.S. Coast Guard activity in the aftermath of two strikes, further corroborating survivor testimony.

QUITO, Ecuador—Alexandra Bravo, the prosecutor assigned to investigate U.S. strikes on three Ecuadorian boats and the 36 survivors’ subsequent accounts of torture and kidnapping, was shot dead in the coastal city of Manta last month. According to police, on June 14 a hitman aboard a black motorcycle opened fire on Bravo as she and her sister were leaving a café at about 11 a.m. Bravo’s sister, who jumped to protect her, was also killed in the attack.

Upon arriving at the crime scene, officers say they found five 9mm shell casings and Bravo’s injured driver, but no sign of the police detail that had been assigned to protect her. The Police Directorate, which operates entirely under the executive branch, has launched a probe to determine if there’d been an internal security breach.

Bravo is the 26th member of Ecuador’s justice system to be assassinated since 2020 and the second individual investigating state crimes murdered that week. Besides her usual caseload of homicide and organized crime, Bravo had been working the Fiorella, Negra Francisca, and Don Maca cases—a series of drone attacks on civilian fishing ships exposed by Drop Site in April. Two of the boat’s crews returned home and reported being abducted, blindfolded, and starved for eight days by American gunmen in U.S. military uniforms aboard a U.S.-flagged patrol ship, before being abandoned in El Salvador. The UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances endorsed the calls for an investigation, demanding that the U.S. provide information on the whereabouts of the eight still-missing men and any involvement in the matter by April 27. To date, the United States has not responded.

Under Ecuador’s right-wing president Daniel Noboa—a Miami-born billionaire often characterized as a “U.S.-backed dictator”—the country has become a central testing ground for Operation Southern Spear, Washington’s extrajudicial bombing campaign purporting to target “narco-terrorists,” which has killed 221 people to date. There is no evidence that many of the victims, including those in Bravo’s investigation, had engaged in drug trafficking.

“I can’t make any assertion regarding it being a political assassination, but evidently, when a prosecutor is killed it’s because of the investigation they’re conducting,” Fernando Bastias, a renowned human rights attorney with Ecuador’s CDH and member of the Geneva-based World Organization Against Torture, told Drop Site, “That’s something we’ve learned from our experience in Ecuador.”

A source inside the Manta police department, who knew Bravo personally, told Drop Site that the Ecuadorian prosecutor was under pressure from her superiors at the Attorney General’s office to treat the U.S. attacks as exclusively “cases of disappearance.” The source, who asked for anonymity out of fear of retaliation, said Bravo was told to close all lines of inquiry after 36 of the 44 missing men were found—despite arriving with severe injuries, including 70% vision loss and feet torn to flesh and bone, which medical experts found consistent with their accounts of explosions and torture.

A senior researcher with Human Rights Watch who interviewed Bravo as part of her investigation into the three vessels, similarly recalled Bravo facing “internal challenges within the institution itself to advance the investigation.” The researcher said the prosecutor repeatedly sought cooperation from other branches responsible for the ship’s rescue, including the Manta Port Captaincy, but “none responded to her requests for information.” During the Negra Francisca bombing, Darwin Pico-Flores, an eyewitness aboard a nearby boat, told Drop Site he called the Manta Port Captaincy to request emergency assistance. Nobody came. In April, as part of its first investigation into the incident, Drop Site called the port seeking comment. Officials hung up after learning the call was from journalists.

As of their last meeting on May 8, the researcher told Drop Site, Bravo “was still in the initial stages of inquiry and investigation.” Bastias said Bravo “was investigating a country [United States] that has been positioned in the media as an ally against crime. That investigation has not advanced at all, and that stems from an intention to avoid getting into trouble or problems with anyone.”

The source inside the Manta Police Department said that, given this lack of cooperation from partner agencies, Bravo had asked for advice on how to pursue new sources for evidence.

In the days leading up to her death, Bravo was relocated to the Attorney General’s office in Montecristi, a neighboring municipality. Her caseload changed after the transfer and she was no longer in charge of investigating the three boat attacks. Drop Site attempted to reach Bravo’s replacement for comment but he had been explicitly instructed not to speak to the press. After weeks of attempts to reach the Attorney General’s office for comment, they told Drop Site the investigation was sealed and they could not comment on why Bravo was relocated.

Inside Ecuador’s U.S.-backed military regime, the Attorney General’s office has become an increasingly opaque and politicized institution. “It’s already a major obstacle for prosecutors to investigate local state agents. Now imagine international state agents,” Bastias said. “The Executive Branch has implemented a series of legal frameworks that leave these foreign state agents immune from prosecution,” he added, referring to the diplomatic immunity granted to all U.S. military and Department of Defense personnel through President Noboa’s 22 martial law decrees.

The Pentagon, Coast Guard, and U.S. Southern Command have all denied any knowledge or responsibility of the boat incidents. After Drop Site published photo evidence of the Negra Francisca bombing, U.S. lawmakers questioned U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth during a congressional hearing. On June 13, the day before Bravo’s murder, Reps. Joaquin Castro (D-Texas) and Bill Keating (D-Mass.) published a letter to Hegseth, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Head of the U.S. Coast Guard, Kevin Lunday, demanding a full audit of U.S. government involvement in the attacks. Despite the deadline of July 10, none of the agencies have issued a public response. Keating’s press secretary Lauren McDermott told Drop Site that his office had received a reply from Rubio’s office, but none from the Department of War or Coast Guard. She did not disclose the contents of the response.

The survivors who returned home, and the families of those who didn’t, still have not received any answers, telling Drop Site “authorities shut the door in our face.” Maria, the wife of one of the fishermen, tells Drop Site her mother-in-law died awaiting her son’s return, saying she was struggling with severe depression and stopped in the weeks leading up to her death.

Despite both governments’ efforts to stonewall the investigation, evidence continues to emerge supporting the fishermen’s accounts of abduction, airstrikes, and torture. Drop Site obtained exclusive video of U.S. Coast Guard activity in the vicinity of the Negra Francisca bombing, open-source intelligence that corroborates the Negra Francisca’s testimonies, and police interviews with eyewitnesses that confirm the U.S. involvement alleged by survivors and documented by Drop Site. With the help of Airwars OSINT analyst and former U.S. Marine Corps member Tomi McCluskey, Drop Site accessed additional NASA thermal imagery consistent with the Negra Francisca bombing and vessel tracking data placing U.S. Coast Guard activity along the route the fishermen say they were taken after the strike.

Video obtained by Drop Site showing alleged Coast Guard activity near the Negra Francisca strike.

Noboa, who governs by military curfews and mass starvation of political prisoners, has gone to great lengths to become Trump’s strongest partner in South America. Since taking office, he brushed aside Ecuador’s constitutional ban on U.S. military presence—ratified by 60% of voters as recently as November 2025—which was originally introduced almost 20 years ago precisely due to a history of U.S. military sinking boats off the coast of Manta. Additionally, his administration authorized the first FBI office on Ecuadorian soil, assisted a U.S. Embassy effort to falsely frame members of Colombia’s left-wing government ahead of elections, and collaborated with the U.S. in the bombing of innocent civilian farmworkers along the Colombian-Ecuadorian border—all in the name of combatting drug trafficking.

Notably, boats from Noboa’s family shipping corporation were caught trafficking ₤26 million of cocaine—a detail that has not deterred the State Department from naming him a key partner in Trump’s War on Drugs. Last month, The Guardian reported that a whistleblower who was investigating Noboa’s ties to drug trafficking was murdered.

Still, Noboa remains a member in good standing of Trump’s Shield of the Americas. The Americas Counter Cartel Coalition, as the Shield is also known, functions as both a military and a highly political alliance, having openly intervened to prop up U.S. interests in Bolivia as President Rodrigo Paz faced off with anti-austery protests.

A local prosecutor charging U.S. forces with extrajudicial bombings and torture of Ecuadorian civilians would undermine the alliance and damage Ecuador-U.S. relations.

Other government officials investigating U.S.-Ecuadorian criminal collusion received death threats. Mónica Palacios, a National Assembly lawmaker representing Ecuadorians living in the United States, who announced plans to bring the Fiorella boat case before the United Nations, faced months of political lawfare after exposing a U.S.-Ecuadorian government embezzlement scandal. Last Friday, Palacios said she received death threats against herself and her one-year-old son, along with footage of the outside of her New York home. She directly blamed President Noboa, saying the threats were retaliation for her investigation into U.S.-Ecuadorian corruption.

“There is a direct persecution of judges and prosecutors who, within the scope of their duties, make decisions that are not entirely aligned with what the Executive Branch wants and end up being sanctioned,” Bastias, the human rights attorney, said. “On the other hand, there is also the risk stemming from the context of criminality.” Regardless, he asserted, Bravo’s death “has a lot to do with what the state does or does not do, because so far there haven’t been any effective security mechanisms for the justice system’s civil servants. The responsibility lies in having failed to ensure protection.”

Diego Vintimilla Jarrín, formerly a lawmaker with Ecuador’s National Assembly and now a spokesperson for Ecuador’s Communist Party, similarly told Drop Site, “Noboa’s government is the most anti-sovereign agenda we have had since the start of democracy. I have no proof of who murdered the prosecutor but the fact that she was investigating certain elements and that they later ceased to seem important also says a lot about the underlying issues.”

The U.S. maintains it never interacted with any of the three boats. A spokesperson for the U.S. Coast Guard told The Guardian that the agency’s only involvement in the events was deploying the USCGC Bertholf on a search-and-rescue mission after receiving a MAYDAY alert that the Negra Francisca was on fire, and ultimately found nothing.

But tracking data of the Bertholf’s movements, provided exclusively to Drop Site by McCluskey, places the cutter near the Negra Francisca around the time of the bombing before turning off its signal—only to reappear off the shore of Costa Rica the same dates the Negra Francisca crew were taken into Central American waters and transferred to El Salvador’s Naval Command, with mangled limbs and major burn injuries from the attack. Hernán Flores, captain of the Negra Francisca, told Drop Site that Salvadoran officers specifically informed him that “U.S. personnel had called to coordinate the handoff.”

The Coast Guard denied that it coordinated the handoff. “The Coast Guard did not play any role in the transfer of fishermen from the Negra Francisca Duarte II,” said a spokesperson.

The USCGC Bertholf departed the Galápagos military base at 4 p.m. on March 16 and stopped transmitting its location shortly afterwards. A day later, the Negra Francisca was bombed 170 miles away—a distance typically covered by boat in 3 to 10 hours. Drop Site asked the U.S. Coast Guard to account for the cutter’s activity after its signal went dark. The Coast Guard responded it “does not disclose cutter movements during law enforcement missions for operational security.”

At 1:02 p.m. on March 17, NASA FIRMS registered a thermal anomaly consistent with an explosive fire, corroborating the time and location where Negra Francisca fishermen told Drop Site their ship was set ablaze by multi-drone strikes. The crew say they were then seized at gunpoint by English-speaking men with blond hair dressed in khaki fatigues with American flag patches stitched onto their sleeves—their descriptions match the uniforms pictured in U.S. Southern Command press releases. Aboard the U.S.-flagged patrol ship, the gunmen allegedly held them hostage, sank their bombed boat, placed hoods over their heads, beat some of the fishermen, and withheld food for eight days as they transported them to Central America.

The USCGC Bertholf’s signal resurfaced in Costa Rican waters on March 22 near the Golfito Port, approximately 450 nautical miles from El Salvador’s waters. It turned off its transponder and did not reactivate it until March 24, 24 hours after El Salvador’s Coast Guard publicly announced having had the Negra Francisca fishermen in their custody.

As part of our first investigation, Drop Site reached out to 11 government personnel in El Salvador. All of them refused to go on the record, citing a media gag order.

There is precedent for the Bertholf transferring victims of U.S. airstrikes to Central American authorities, with Costa Rican outlets reporting it delivered the remains of two deceased and one injured survivor to Costa Rica’s Port of Golfito around the same time. Costa Rica’s nautical inspector Wilber Urroz Guido said he had no information on the cutter’s movements but that it was authorized to act under a memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Costa Rica—similar to agreements the U.S. maintains with Ecuador and El Salvador.

Eyewitness testimony also casts doubt on the U.S. Coast Guard’s version of events. Video footage shared exclusively with Drop Site by Darwin Flores-Pico, an eyewitness to the attack and nephew of the Negra Francisca’s captain, shows a U.S. Coast Guard cutter patrolling the waters where the bombing occurred.

Video obtained by Drop Site showing alleged Coast Guard activity near the Negra Francisca strike.

Darwin said he was fishing nearby on March 17, aboard his boat the Solavil, when he spotted smoke rising in the distance around 2 p.m. While making repeated attempts to reach the Negra Francisca’s crew by radio, he spotted an American aircraft circling above. It wasn’t until hours later that he learned by radio signal that the Negra Francisca was in flames and rushed to make his way to the scene, finding the vessel consumed by fire and no sign of survivors.

He recovered two scorched emergency skiffs, took photo evidence of the fire, then called the Port of Manta to ask for help. Nobody came.

Darwin decided to begin his journey back to the port to get emergency assistance and, as he was leaving the scene of the fire, red and green lights descended upon the Negra Francisca. Fearing for his safety, he steered his boat away from the site.

The following afternoon, Darwin told Drop Site his boat was boarded by the U.S. Coast Guard, which detained and questioned the crew for nearly 12 hours via a Spanish translator with a Puerto Rican accent. He said Coast Guard personnel confirmed the red and green lights were from their patrol and acknowledged reaching the site of the Negra Francisca the previous night, but refused to elaborate on anything they’d found.

Instead, they questioned the fishermen about whether they’d seen anything and why Darwin had salvaged the skiffs. After telling the Coast Guard officials that the Negra Francisca was his uncle’s boat, Darwin says they abruptly stopped questioning him and began communicating by radio in English with colleagues aboard the nearby cutter shown in the video. “Since we were the only people who saw everything, we were afraid they might do something to us,” Darwin said. He felt the U.S. Coast Guard showed little interest in helping him locate his family and instead seemed more focused on “making sure we weren’t witnesses to anything.”

McCluskey says the multi-drone tactic—described by all three boats—reflects a U.S. doctrine. He argues it’s unlikely that other regional powers, from neighboring countries to organized crime groups, would have the budget or access for such technology. There is no known precedent of cartels using “eye-in-the-sky” surveillance drones deep in maritime territory, though the Coast Guard has also denied operating armed drones in Ecuadorian waters.

Furthermore, the decision to keep the survivors alive, albeit involving testimonies of torture, and the efforts and expenses to transport them, is far more reflective of a Department of Defense protocol—-designed to avoid international legal ramifications—than any organized crime group would typically care to practice. “If it was cartels, you would’ve never found them,” McCluskey said. “There would be no survivors to talk to, there would be no stories.”

The Fiorella was struck off the coast of the Galápagos on January 20; all eight fishermen aboard remain missing. The day before the vessel vanished, the captain’s wife received a call from her husband on an emergency line, warning that U.S. aircraft were orbiting overhead.

Drop Site obtained police interview transcripts from two eyewitnesses, Christian Flores and Dimas Ignacio Álvarez, who corroborated seeing the Fiorella engulfed in smoke and surrounded by American assets. The two men were members of the Fiorella crew but had been out setting a long line on a nearby raft for several hours when the vessel went up in smoke.

In their police statements, Flores and Álvarez described two U.S. aircraft flying over the Fiorella on January 18; multiple grey American drones and a U.S.-flagged patrol ship circling the vessel on January 19; and, on January 20—the day their crewmates disappeared—the large U.S.-flagged patrol ship near the smoke. From a distance, they could not make out the personnel aboard the ship, but their accounts echo those of the Negra Francisca crew, who said they were taken hostage by armed Americans aboard a U.S.-flagged patrol vessel. The witnesses’ descriptions also match aircraft and equipment featured in public posts by U.S. Southern Command.

After spotting the smoke, the two fishermen said they heard their crewmates calling the captain over the radio in distress. They were never seen again.

The attorney representing the two survivors of the Fiorella, Juan Avila, told Drop Site that the slain prosecutor, Alexandra Bravo, was in fact his niece.

The Coast Guard told Drop Site it “has no record of involvement with La Fiorella.”

The absence of an assigned police detail when Bravo was murdered bears similarities to the 2023 assassination of frontrunner presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio. A congressional commission determined that Villavicencio’s police detail was insufficient, that he had been unconventionally escorted through an exposed street-level exit contrary to standard protocol, and that the armored vehicle designated to protect Villavicencio on the campaign trail had been left by his security team in another city that day. These breaches made him particularly vulnerable when assailants approached and shot him on the sidewalk as he was leaving a meeting with other government officials.

Villavicencio’s death cleared the way for now-President Daniel Noboa’s campaign—which had been polling at 3%—to surge to victory. In an interview with Señal Colombia, National Assembly legislator and member of Villavicencio’s party, Gisella Molina, who was with him and injured during the assassination, suggested government officials had prior knowledge of the plot.

During the 2024 murder investigation, Drop Site published private messages from then–Attorney General Diana Salazar revealing a plot to implicate former democratic socialist President Correa’s party in Villavicencio’s assassination, amid close collaboration with the U.S. ambassador.

The state later concluded that the Los Lobos cartel carried out Villavicencio’s murder and alleged that former members of Correa’s party were the masterminds. Prosecutors assert that Los Lobos killed Villavicencio for exposing their criminal network. While Villavicencio campaigned on eradicating the cartel economy, Ecuador under Noboa—accused of offering organized crime bosses immunity in exchange for electoral support—has risen as the top distribution hub for 70% of the world’s cocaine.

Immediately following Bravo’s death, the Attorney General issued a public statement attributing her murder to retaliation against prosecutors combating organized crime. When asked why authorities had linked the killing to organized crime and whether investigators had uncovered any information about Bravo’s missing police protection detail, the Attorney General’s office told Drop Site the investigation is under seal and declined to comment.

Though the attorney general has yet to present evidence to support their claim, Bravo lamented to the Human Rights Watch that “danger was always present” in her work. “She said that being a prosecutor in a context of organized crime was complex and risky, but she did not provide any further details,” the researcher told Drop Site. Manta sits at the epicenter of Ecuador’s organized crime crisis, as the small South American country becomes the most violent nation in the Western Hemisphere.

Bravo was also responsible for looking into the unsolved 2024 disappearance of the Patricia Lynn ship and its 21 crew members.

Bravo is the second person associated with the Patricia Lynn case to be assassinated. The first was the mother-in-law of one of the disappeared fishermen who became the spokesperson for the victims’ families and organized marches demanding answers for their missing relatives. María Chóez was fatally shot by two armed assailants while operating her street food stand in downtown Manta.

The Human Rights Watch researcher says the sinking of the Patricia Lynn boat in Ecuadorian waters, “served as a precedent in all these ship-related matters.”

“If Ecuador had a framework of trust in its institutions, one might think [Bravo’s murder] was an ordinary crime,” Vintimilla Jarrin, the former lawmaker, said. “But given the systematic violence against judges, prosecutors, and lawyers, there isn’t much room to give them the benefit of the doubt. Twenty-six murdered members of the justice system is a shocking number. And of course, this entire crisis has been fostered by an agenda driven directly by government authorities; the ones who benefit from organized crime are the large power groups.”

Hernán Flores, captain of the Negra Francisca, told Drop Site that Salvadoran officers specifically informed him that “U.S. personnel had called to coordinate the handoff.”The Coast Guard denied that it coordinated the handoff. “The Coast Guard did not play any role in the transfer of fishermen from the Negra Francisca Duarte II,” said a spokesperson.The USCGC Bertholf operating in Costa Rican waters on the same dates (times converted from UTC) that the Negra Francisca crew members were brought to Central America and received by El Salvador’s Navy/Coast Guard. Photo from Global Fishing Watch, provided by OSINT analyst Tomi McCluskey.The USCGC Bertholf departed the Galápagos military base at 4 p.m. on March 16 and stopped transmitting its location shortly afterwards. A day later, the Negra Francisca was bombed 170 miles away—a distance typically covered by boat in 3 to 10 hours. Drop Site asked the U.S. Coast Guard to account for the cutter’s activity after its signal went dark. The Coast Guard responded it “does not disclose cutter movements during law enforcement missions for operational security.”At 1:02 p.m. on March 17, NASA FIRMS registered a thermal anomaly consistent with an explosive fire, corroborating the time and location where Negra Francisca fishermen told Drop Site their ship was set ablaze by multi-drone strikes. The crew say they were then seized at gunpoint by English-speaking men with blond hair dressed in khaki fatigues with American flag patches stitched onto their sleeves—their descriptions match the uniforms pictured in U.S. Southern Command press releases. Aboard the U.S.-flagged patrol ship, the gunmen allegedly held them hostage, sank their bombed boat, placed hoods over their heads, beat some of the fishermen, and withheld food for eight days as they transported them to Central America.OSINT provided to Drop Site by Tomi McCluskey document the USCGC Bertholf’s movements near the Negra Francisca around the time of the bombing (times converted from UTC).OSINT provided to Drop Site by Tomi McCluskey documenting the USCGC Bertholf’s movements near the Negra Francisca around the time of the bombing (times converted from UTC).The USCGC Bertholf’s signal resurfaced in Costa Rican waters on March 22 near the Golfito Port, approximately 450 nautical miles from El Salvador’s waters. It turned off its transponder and did not reactivate it until March 24, 24 hours after El Salvador’s Coast Guard publicly announced having had the Negra Francisca fishermen in their custody.As part of our first investigation, Drop Site reached out to 11 government personnel in El Salvador. All of them refused to go on the record, citing a media gag order.There is precedent for the Bertholf transferring victims of U.S. airstrikes to Central American authorities, with Costa Rican outlets reporting it delivered the remains of two deceased and one injured survivor to Costa Rica’s Port of Golfito around the same time. Costa Rica’s nautical inspector Wilber Urroz Guido said he had no information on the cutter’s movements but that it was authorized to act under a memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Costa Rica—similar to agreements the U.S. maintains with Ecuador and El Salvador.Eyewitness testimony also casts doubt on the U.S. Coast Guard’s version of events. Video footage shared exclusively with Drop Site by Darwin Flores-Pico, an eyewitness to the attack and nephew of the Negra Francisca’s captain, shows a U.S. Coast Guard cutter patrolling the waters where the bombing occurred.Video obtained by Drop Site showing alleged Coast Guard activity near the Negra Francisca strike.Darwin said he was fishing nearby on March 17, aboard his boat the Solavil, when he spotted smoke rising in the distance around 2 p.m. While making repeated attempts to reach the Negra Francisca’s crew by radio, he spotted an American aircraft circling above. It wasn’t until hours later that he learned by radio signal that the Negra Francisca was in flames and rushed to make his way to the scene, finding the vessel consumed by fire and no sign of survivors.He recovered two scorched emergency skiffs, took photo evidence of the fire, then called the Port of Manta to ask for help. Nobody came.Darwin decided to begin his journey back to the port to get emergency assistance and, as he was leaving the scene of the fire, red and green lights descended upon the Negra Francisca. Fearing for his safety, he steered his boat away from the site.The Negra Francisca burning, photographed and shared with Drop Site by Darwin Pico-Flores.The following afternoon, Darwin told Drop Site his boat was boarded by the U.S. Coast Guard, which detained and questioned the crew for nearly 12 hours via a Spanish translator with a Puerto Rican accent. He said Coast Guard personnel confirmed the red and green lights were from their patrol and acknowledged reaching the site of the Negra Francisca the previous night, but refused to elaborate on anything they’d found.Instead, they questioned the fishermen about whether they’d seen anything and why Darwin had salvaged the skiffs. After telling the Coast Guard officials that the Negra Francisca was his uncle’s boat, Darwin says they abruptly stopped questioning him and began communicating by radio in English with colleagues aboard the nearby cutter shown in the video. “Since we were the only people who saw everything, we were afraid they might do something to us,” Darwin said. He felt the U.S. Coast Guard showed little interest in helping him locate his family and instead seemed more focused on “making sure we weren’t witnesses to anything.”McCluskey says the multi-drone tactic—described by all three boats—reflects a U.S. doctrine. He argues it’s unlikely that other regional powers, from neighboring countries to organized crime groups, would have the budget or access for such technology. There is no known precedent of cartels using “eye-in-the-sky” surveillance drones deep in maritime territory, though the Coast Guard has also denied operating armed drones in Ecuadorian waters.Furthermore, the decision to keep the survivors alive, albeit involving testimonies of torture, and the efforts and expenses to transport them, is far more reflective of a Department of Defense protocol—-designed to avoid international legal ramifications—than any organized crime group would typically care to practice. “If it was cartels, you would’ve never found them,” McCluskey said. “There would be no survivors to talk to, there would be no stories.”The Fiorella was struck off the coast of the Galápagos on January 20; all eight fishermen aboard remain missing. The day before the vessel vanished, the captain’s wife received a call from her husband on an emergency line, warning that U.S. aircraft were orbiting overhead.Drop Site obtained police interview transcripts from two eyewitnesses, Christian Flores and Dimas Ignacio Álvarez, who corroborated seeing the Fiorella engulfed in smoke and surrounded by American assets. The two men were members of the Fiorella crew but had been out setting a long line on a nearby raft for several hours when the vessel went up in smoke.In their police statements, Flores and Álvarez described two U.S. aircraft flying over the Fiorella on January 18; multiple grey American drones and a U.S.-flagged patrol ship circling the vessel on January 19; and, on January 20—the day their crewmates disappeared—the large U.S.-flagged patrol ship near the smoke. From a distance, they could not make out the personnel aboard the ship, but their accounts echo those of the Negra Francisca crew, who said they were taken hostage by armed Americans aboard a U.S.-flagged patrol vessel. The witnesses’ descriptions also match aircraft and equipment featured in public posts by U.S. Southern Command.Transcripts of police interviews with the eyewitnesses, obtained exclusively by Drop Site News. Originals in Spanish, translated copies in English.After spotting the smoke, the two fishermen said they heard their crewmates calling the captain over the radio in distress. They were never seen again.The attorney representing the two survivors of the Fiorella, Juan Avila, told Drop Site that the slain prosecutor, Alexandra Bravo, was in fact his niece.The Coast Guard told Drop Site it “has no record of involvement with La Fiorella.”The absence of an assigned police detail when Bravo was murdered bears similarities to the 2023 assassination of frontrunner presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio. A congressional commission determined that Villavicencio’s police detail was insufficient, that he had been unconventionally escorted through an exposed street-level exit contrary to standard protocol, and that the armored vehicle designated to protect Villavicencio on the campaign trail had been left by his security team in another city that day. These breaches made him particularly vulnerable when assailants approached and shot him on the sidewalk as he was leaving a meeting with other government officials.Villavicencio’s death cleared the way for now-President Daniel Noboa’s campaign—which had been polling at 3%—to surge to victory. In an interview with Señal Colombia, National Assembly legislator and member of Villavicencio’s party, Gisella Molina, who was with him and injured during the assassination, suggested government officials had prior knowledge of the plot.During the 2024 murder investigation, Drop Site published private messages from then–Attorney General Diana Salazar revealing a plot to implicate former democratic socialist President Correa’s party in Villavicencio’s assassination, amid close collaboration with the U.S. ambassador.The state later concluded that the Los Lobos cartel carried out Villavicencio’s murder and alleged that former members of Correa’s party were the masterminds. Prosecutors assert that Los Lobos killed Villavicencio for exposing their criminal network. While Villavicencio campaigned on eradicating the cartel economy, Ecuador under Noboa—accused of offering organized crime bosses immunity in exchange for electoral support—has risen as the top distribution hub for 70% of the world’s cocaine.Immediately following Bravo’s death, the Attorney General issued a public statement attributing her murder to retaliation against prosecutors combating organized crime. When asked why authorities had linked the killing to organized crime and whether investigators had uncovered any information about Bravo’s missing police protection detail, the Attorney General’s office told Drop Site the investigation is under seal and declined to comment.Though the attorney general has yet to present evidence to support their claim, Bravo lamented to the Human Rights Watch that “danger was always present” in her work. “She said that being a prosecutor in a context of organized crime was complex and risky, but she did not provide any further details,” the researcher told Drop Site. Manta sits at the epicenter of Ecuador’s organized crime crisis, as the small South American country becomes the most violent nation in the Western Hemisphere.Bravo was also responsible for looking into the unsolved 2024 disappearance of the Patricia Lynn ship and its 21 crew members.Bravo is the second person associated with the Patricia Lynn case to be assassinated. The first was the mother-in-law of one of the disappeared fishermen who became the spokesperson for the victims’ families and organized marches demanding answers for their missing relatives. María Chóez was fatally shot by two armed assailants while operating her street food stand in downtown Manta.The Human Rights Watch researcher says the sinking of the Patricia Lynn boat in Ecuadorian waters, “served as a precedent in all these ship-related matters.”“If Ecuador had a framework of trust in its institutions, one might think [Bravo’s murder] was an ordinary crime,” Vintimilla Jarrin, the former lawmaker, said. “But given the systematic violence against judges, prosecutors, and lawyers, there isn’t much room to give them the benefit of the doubt. Twenty-six murdered members of the justice system is a shocking number. And of course, this entire crisis has been fostered by an agenda driven directly by government authorities; the ones who benefit from organized crime are the large power groups.”Leave a commentShare

blocks.html_en: QUITO, Ecuador—Alexandra Bravo, the prosecutor assigned to investigate U.S. strikes on three Ecuadorian boats and the 36 survivors’ subsequent accounts of torture and kidnapping, was shot dead in the coastal city of Manta last month. According to police, on June 14 a hitman aboard a black motorcycle opened fire on Bravo as she and her sister were leaving a café at about 11 a.m. Bravo’s sister, who jumped to protect her, was also killed in the attack.

blocks.html_en: Bravo is the 26th member of Ecuador’s justice system to be assassinated since 2020 and the second individual investigating state crimes murdered that week. Besides her usual caseload of homicide and organized crime, Bravo had been working the Fiorella, Negra Francisca, and Don Maca cases—a series of drone attacks on civilian fishing ships exposed by Drop Site in April. Two of the boat’s crews returned home and reported being abducted, blindfolded, and starved for eight days by American gunmen in U.S. military uniforms aboard a U.S.-flagged patrol ship, before being abandoned in El Salvador. The UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances endorsed the calls for an investigation, demanding that the U.S. provide information on the whereabouts of the eight still-missing men and any involvement in the matter by April 27. To date, the United States has not responded.

There is no evidence that many of the victims, including those in Bravo’s investigation, had engaged in drug trafficking.

sentences.zh: 空投点要求美国海岸警卫队对快艇信号消失后的活动进行解释。

sentences.en: The Coast Guard responded it “does not disclose cutter movements during law enforcement missions for operational security.”
sentences.zh: 海岸警卫队回应称，“出于行动安全考虑，不会披露执法任务期间的巡逻艇动向”。

blocks.html_en: At 1:02 p.m. on March 17, NASA FIRMS registered a thermal anomaly consistent with an explosive fire, corroborating the time and location where Negra Francisca fishermen told Drop Site their ship was set ablaze by multi-drone strikes. The crew say they were then seized at gunpoint by English-speaking men with blond hair dressed in khaki fatigues with American flag patches stitched onto their sleeves—their descriptions match the uniforms pictured in U.S. Southern Command press releases. Aboard the U.S.-flagged patrol ship, the gunmen allegedly held them hostage, sank their bombed boat, placed hoods over their heads, beat some of the fishermen, and withheld food for eight days as they transported them to Central America.

sentences.en: At 1:02 p.m.

on March 17, NASA FIRMS registered a thermal anomaly consistent with an explosive fire, corroborating the time and location where Negra Francisca fishermen told Drop Site their ship was set ablaze by multi-drone strikes.
sentences.zh: 3 月 17 日，NASA FIRMS 记录到了与爆炸性火灾一致的热异常现象，证实了 Negra Francisca 渔民告诉 Drop Site 他们的船被多架无人机袭击起火的时间和地点。

sentences.en: The crew say they were then seized at gunpoint by English-speaking men with blond hair dressed in khaki fatigues with American flag patches stitched onto their sleeves—their descriptions match the uniforms pictured in U.S. Southern Command press releases.
sentences.zh: 机组人员表示，他们随后被身穿卡其布迷彩服、袖子上缝有美国国旗补丁的金发英语男子用枪指着——他们的描述与美国南方司令部新闻稿中的制服相符。

sentences.en: Aboard the U.S.-flagged patrol ship, the gunmen allegedly held them hostage, sank their bombed boat, placed hoods over their heads, beat some of the fishermen, and withheld food for eight days as they transported them to Central America.
sentences.zh: 据称，在这艘悬挂美国国旗的巡逻船上，枪手将他们扣为人质，击沉了被炸毁的船只，用头罩蒙住他们的头，殴打了一些渔民，并在将他们运往中美洲的过程中扣留了八天的食物。

blocks.html_en: The USCGC Bertholf’s signal resurfaced in Costa Rican waters on March 22 near the Golfito Port, approximately 450 nautical miles from El Salvador’s waters. It turned off its transponder and did not reactivate it until March 24, 24 hours after El Salvador’s Coast Guard publicly announced having had the Negra Francisca fishermen in their custody.

sentences.en: The USCGC Bertholf’s signal resurfaced in Costa Rican waters on March 22 near the Golfito Port, approximately 450 nautical miles from El Salvador’s waters.
sentences.zh: 3 月 22 日，USCGC Bertholf 的信号在戈尔菲托港附近的哥斯达黎加水域重新出现，距离萨尔瓦多水域约 450 海里。

sentences.en: It turned off its transponder and did not reactivate it until March 24, 24 hours after El Salvador’s Coast Guard publicly announced having had the Negra Francisca fishermen in their custody.
sentences.zh: 它关闭了应答器，直到 3 月 24 日才重新启动，即萨尔瓦多海岸警卫队公开宣布拘留 Negra Francisca 渔民 24 小时后。

blocks.html_en: As part of our first investigation, Drop Site reached out to 11 government personnel in El Salvador. All of them refused to go on the record, citing a media gag order.

sentences.en: As part of our first investigation, Drop Site reached out to 11 government personnel in El Salvador.
sentences.zh: 作为我们首次调查的一部分，Drop Site 联系了萨尔瓦多的 11 名政府人员。

sentences.en: All of them refused to go on the record, citing a media gag order.
sentences.zh: 他们都以媒体禁言令为由拒绝公开记录。

blocks.html_en: There is precedent for the Bertholf transferring victims of U.S. airstrikes to Central American authorities, with Costa Rican outlets reporting it delivered the remains of two deceased and one injured survivor to Costa Rica’s Port of Golfito around the same time. Costa Rica’s nautical inspector Wilber Urroz Guido said he had no information on the cutter’s movements but that it was authorized to act under a memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Costa Rica—similar to agreements the U.S. maintains with Ecuador and El Salvador.

sentences.en: There is precedent for the Bertholf transferring victims of U.S. airstrikes to Central American authorities, with Costa Rican outlets reporting it delivered the remains of two deceased and one injured survivor to Costa Rica’s Port of Golfito around the same time.
sentences.zh: 伯索夫号曾有先例将美国空袭的受害者转移给中美洲当局，哥斯达黎加媒体报道称，该船大约在同一时间将两名死者和一名受伤幸存者的遗体运送到哥斯达黎加的戈尔菲托港。

sentences.en: Costa Rica’s nautical inspector Wilber Urroz Guido said he had no information on the cutter’s movements but that it was authorized to act under a memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Costa Rica—similar to agreements the U.S. maintains with Ecuador and El Salvador.
sentences.zh: 哥斯达黎加海事检查员威尔伯·乌罗兹·吉多(Wilber Urroz Guido)表示，他不知道这艘快艇的动向，但它被授权根据美国和哥斯达黎加之间的谅解备忘录采取行动，类似于美国与厄瓜多尔和萨尔瓦多维持的协议。

blocks.html_en: Eyewitness testimony also casts doubt on the U.S. Coast Guard’s version of events. Video footage shared exclusively with Drop Site by Darwin Flores-Pico, an eyewitness to the attack and nephew of the Negra Francisca’s captain, shows a U.S. Coast Guard cutter patrolling the waters where the bombing occurred.

sentences.en: Eyewitness testimony also casts doubt on the U.S. Coast Guard’s version of events.
sentences.zh: 目击者的证词也让人对美国海岸警卫队对事件的描述产生怀疑。

sentences.en: Video footage shared exclusively with Drop Site by Darwin Flores-Pico, an eyewitness to the attack and nephew of the Negra Francisca’s captain, shows a U.S. Coast Guard cutter patrolling the waters where the bombing occurred.
sentences.zh: 袭击事件目击者、内格拉·弗朗西斯卡船长的侄子达尔文·弗洛雷斯-皮科 (Darwin Flores-Pico) 与 Drop Site 独家分享的视频片段显示，一艘美国海岸警卫队快艇正在爆炸发生的水域巡逻。

blocks.html_en: Video obtained by Drop Site showing alleged Coast Guard activity near the Negra Francisca strike.

sentences.en: Video obtained by Drop Site showing alleged Coast Guard activity near the Negra Francisca strike.
sentences.zh: Drop Site 获得的视频显示，据称海岸警卫队在 Negra Francisca 罢工附近活动。

blocks.html_en: Darwin said he was fishing nearby on March 17, aboard his boat the Solavil, when he spotted smoke rising in the distance around 2 p.m. While making repeated attempts to reach the Negra Francisca’s crew by radio, he spotted an American aircraft circling above. It wasn’t until hours later that he learned by radio signal that the Negra Francisca was in flames and rushed to make his way to the scene, finding the vessel consumed by fire and no sign of survivors.

sentences.en: Darwin said he was fishing nearby on March 17, aboard his boat the Solavil, when he spotted smoke rising in the distance around 2 p.m.
sentences.zh: 达尔文说，3 月 17 日，他在附近的 Solavil 号船上钓鱼，下午 2 点左右，他发现远处升起浓烟。

sentences.en: While making repeated attempts to reach the Negra Francisca’s crew by radio, he spotted an American aircraft circling above.
sentences.zh: 当他多次尝试通过无线电联系内格拉·弗朗西斯卡号的机组人员时，他发现一架美国飞机在上空盘旋。

sentences.en: It wasn’t until hours later that he learned by radio signal that the Negra Francisca was in flames and rushed to make his way to the scene, finding the vessel consumed by fire and no sign of survivors.
sentences.zh: 直到几个小时后，他才通过无线电信号得知“内格拉·弗朗西斯卡”号起火了，于是他赶到现场，发现船只已被大火吞噬，没有幸存者的迹象。

blocks.html_en: He recovered two scorched emergency skiffs, took photo evidence of the fire, then called the Port of Manta to ask for help. Nobody came.

sentences.en: He recovered two scorched emergency skiffs, took photo evidence of the fire, then called the Port of Manta to ask for help.
sentences.zh: 他找到了两艘烧焦的应急船，拍下了火灾的照片证据，然后致电曼塔港寻求帮助。

sentences.en: Nobody came.
sentences.zh: 没有人来。

blocks.html_en: Darwin decided to begin his journey back to the port to get emergency assistance and, as he was leaving the scene of the fire, red and green lights descended upon the Negra Francisca. Fearing for his safety, he steered his boat away from the site.

sentences.en: Darwin decided to begin his journey back to the port to get emergency assistance and, as he was leaving the scene of the fire, red and green lights descended upon the Negra Francisca.
sentences.zh: 达尔文决定开始返回港口寻求紧急援助，当他离开火灾现场时，红色和绿色的灯光落在了内格拉·弗朗西斯卡号上。

sentences.en: Fearing for his safety, he steered his boat away from the site.
sentences.zh: 由于担心自己的安全，他将船驶离了现场。

sentences.en: The Negra Francisca burning, photographed and shared with Drop Site by Darwin Pico-Flores.
sentences.zh: 燃烧的内格拉·弗朗西斯卡 (Negra Francisca) 被达尔文·皮科·弗洛雷斯 (Darwin Pico-Flores) 拍摄并与 Drop Site 分享。

blocks.html_en: The following afternoon, Darwin told Drop Site his boat was boarded by the U.S. Coast Guard, which detained and questioned the crew for nearly 12 hours via a Spanish translator with a Puerto Rican accent. He said Coast Guard personnel confirmed the red and green lights were from their patrol and acknowledged reaching the site of the Negra Francisca the previous night, but refused to elaborate on anything they’d found.

sentences.en: The following afternoon, Darwin told Drop Site his boat was boarded by the U.S. Coast Guard, which detained and questioned the crew for nearly 12 hours via a Spanish translator with a Puerto Rican accent.
sentences.zh: 第二天下午，达尔文告诉 Drop Site，他的船被美国海岸警卫队登上，美国海岸警卫队通过带有波多黎各口音的西班牙语翻译拘留并审问了船员近 12 个小时。

sentences.en: He said Coast Guard personnel confirmed the red and green lights were from their patrol and acknowledged reaching the site of the Negra Francisca the previous night, but refused to elaborate on anything they’d found.
sentences.zh: 他说，海岸警卫队人员确认红灯和绿灯来自他们的巡逻队，并承认前一天晚上到达了内格拉·弗朗西斯卡号的现场，但拒绝详细说明他们发现的任何内容。

blocks.html_en: Instead, they questioned the fishermen about whether they’d seen anything and why Darwin had salvaged the skiffs. After telling the Coast Guard officials that the Negra Francisca was his uncle’s boat, Darwin says they abruptly stopped questioning him and began communicating by radio in English with colleagues aboard the nearby cutter shown in the video. “Since we were the only people who saw everything, we were afraid they might do something to us,” Darwin said. He felt the U.S. Coast Guard showed little interest in helping him locate his family and instead seemed more focused on “making sure we weren’t witnesses to anything.”

sentences.en: Instead, they questioned the fishermen about whether they’d seen anything and why Darwin had salvaged the skiffs.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们询问渔民是否看到任何东西以及达尔文为何打捞小船。

sentences.en: After telling the Coast Guard officials that the Negra Francisca was his uncle’s boat, Darwin says they abruptly stopped questioning him and began communicating by radio in English with colleagues aboard the nearby cutter shown in the video.
sentences.zh: 达尔文说，在告诉海岸警卫队官员内格拉·弗朗西斯卡号是他叔叔的船后，他们突然停止询问他，并开始用英语通过无线电与视频中显示的附近快艇上的同事进行交流。

sentences.en: “Since we were the only people who saw everything, we were afraid they might do something to us,” Darwin said.
sentences.zh: 达尔文说：“由于我们是唯一看到一切的人，我们担心他们可能会对我们做点什么。”

sentences.en: He felt the U.S. Coast Guard showed little interest in helping him locate his family and instead seemed more focused on “making sure we weren’t witnesses to anything.”
sentences.zh: 他觉得美国海岸警卫队对帮助他找到家人没有兴趣，而是似乎更专注于“确保我们不是任何事情的目击者”。

blocks.html_en: McCluskey says the multi-drone tactic—described by all three boats—reflects a U.S. doctrine. He argues it’s unlikely that other regional powers, from neighboring countries to organized crime groups, would have the budget or access for such technology. There is no known precedent of cartels using “eye-in-the-sky” surveillance drones deep in maritime territory, though the Coast Guard has also denied operating armed drones in Ecuadorian waters.

sentences.en: McCluskey says the multi-drone tactic—described by all three boats—reflects a U.S. doctrine.
sentences.zh: 麦克拉斯基说，三艘船所描述的多无人机战术反映了美国的原则。

sentences.en: He argues it’s unlikely that other regional powers, from neighboring countries to organized crime groups, would have the budget or access for such technology.
sentences.zh: 他认为，从邻国到有组织犯罪集团的其他地区大国不太可能有预算或获得此类技术。

sentences.en: There is no known precedent of cartels using “eye-in-the-sky” surveillance drones deep in maritime territory, though the Coast Guard has also denied operating armed drones in Ecuadorian waters.
sentences.zh: 尽管海岸警卫队也否认在厄瓜多尔水域使用武装无人机，但卡特尔在海域深处使用“天眼”监视无人机尚无先例。

blocks.html_en: Furthermore, the decision to keep the survivors alive, albeit involving testimonies of torture, and the efforts and expenses to transport them, is far more reflective of a Department of Defense protocol—-designed to avoid international legal ramifications—than any organized crime group would typically care to practice. “If it was cartels, you would’ve never found them,” McCluskey said. “There would be no survivors to talk to, there would be no stories.”

sentences.en: Furthermore, the decision to keep the survivors alive, albeit involving testimonies of torture, and the efforts and expenses to transport them, is far more reflective of a Department of Defense protocol—-designed to avoid international legal ramifications—than any organized crime group would typically care to practice.
sentences.zh: 此外，让幸存者活着的决定，尽管涉及酷刑证词，以及运送他们的努力和费用，比任何有组织犯罪集团通常愿意采取的做法更能反映国防部的协议——旨在避免国际法律后果。

sentences.en: “If it was cartels, you would’ve never found them,” McCluskey said.
sentences.zh: “如果是卡特尔，你永远找不到他们，”麦克拉斯基说。

sentences.en: “There would be no survivors to talk to, there would be no stories.”
sentences.zh: “不会有幸存者可以交谈，不会有故事。”

blocks.html_en: The Fiorella was struck off the coast of the Galápagos on January 20; all eight fishermen aboard remain missing. The day before the vessel vanished, the captain’s wife received a call from her husband on an emergency line, warning that U.S. aircraft were orbiting overhead.

sentences.en: The Fiorella was struck off the coast of the Galápagos on January 20; all eight fishermen aboard remain missing.
sentences.zh: “菲奥雷拉”号于 1 月 20 日在加拉帕戈斯群岛海岸被击中；船上八名渔民全部失踪。

sentences.en: The day before the vessel vanished, the captain’s wife received a call from her husband on an emergency line, warning that U.S. aircraft were orbiting overhead.
sentences.zh: 船只消失的前一天，船长的妻子接到丈夫打来的紧急电话，警告美国飞机正在上空盘旋。

blocks.html_en: Drop Site obtained police interview transcripts from two eyewitnesses, Christian Flores and Dimas Ignacio Álvarez, who corroborated seeing the Fiorella engulfed in smoke and surrounded by American assets. The two men were members of the Fiorella crew but had been out setting a long line on a nearby raft for several hours when the vessel went up in smoke.

sentences.en: Drop Site obtained police interview transcripts from two eyewitnesses, Christian Flores and Dimas Ignacio Álvarez, who corroborated seeing the Fiorella engulfed in smoke and surrounded by American assets.
sentences.zh: Drop Site 从两名目击者克里斯蒂安·弗洛雷斯 (Christian Flores) 和迪马斯·伊格纳西奥·阿尔瓦雷斯 (Dimas Ignacio Álvarez) 那里获得了警方的采访笔录，他们证实看到菲奥雷拉号被烟雾吞没，并被美国资产包围。

sentences.en: The two men were members of the Fiorella crew but had been out setting a long line on a nearby raft for several hours when the vessel went up in smoke.
sentences.zh: 这两名男子是“菲奥雷拉”号船员，但在附近的一艘木筏上拉长绳几个小时后，船只冒烟了。

blocks.html_en: In their police statements, Flores and Álvarez described two U.S. aircraft flying over the Fiorella on January 18; multiple grey American drones and a U.S.-flagged patrol ship circling the vessel on January 19; and, on January 20—the day their crewmates disappeared—the large U.S.-flagged patrol ship near the smoke. From a distance, they could not make out the personnel aboard the ship, but their accounts echo those of the Negra Francisca crew, who said they were taken hostage by armed Americans aboard a U.S.-flagged patrol vessel. The witnesses’ descriptions also match aircraft and equipment featured in public posts by U.S. Southern Command.

sentences.en: In their police statements, Flores and Álvarez described two U.S. aircraft flying over the Fiorella on January 18; multiple grey American drones and a U.S.-flagged patrol ship circling the vessel on January 19; and, on January 20—the day their crewmates disappeared—the large U.S.-flagged patrol ship near the smoke.
sentences.zh: 弗洛雷斯和阿尔瓦雷斯在警方声明中描述了 1 月 18 日两架美国飞机飞越菲奥雷拉上空的情况； 1月19日，多架灰色美国无人机和一艘悬挂美国国旗的巡逻舰在该船周围盘旋； 1 月 20 日——他们的船员失踪的那一天——一艘悬挂美国国旗的大型巡逻船在烟雾附近。

sentences.en: From a distance, they could not make out the personnel aboard the ship, but their accounts echo those of the Negra Francisca crew, who said they were taken hostage by armed Americans aboard a U.S.-flagged patrol vessel.
sentences.zh: 从远处看，他们无法辨认船上的人员，但他们的说法与“内格拉·弗朗西斯卡”号船员的说法相呼应，他们说，他们在一艘悬挂美国国旗的巡逻船上被武装的美国人扣为人质。

sentences.en: The witnesses’ descriptions also match aircraft and equipment featured in public posts by U.S. Southern Command.
sentences.zh: 目击者的描述也与美国南方司令部公开帖子中介绍的飞机和设备相符。

blocks.html_en: After spotting the smoke, the two fishermen said they heard their crewmates calling the captain over the radio in distress. They were never seen again.

sentences.zh: 发现烟雾后，两名渔民表示，他们听到船员通过无线电向船长求救。

sentences.en: They were never seen again.
sentences.zh: 他们再也没有被见过。

blocks.html_en: The attorney representing the two survivors of the Fiorella, Juan Avila, told Drop Site that the slain prosecutor, Alexandra Bravo, was in fact his niece.

sentences.zh: 代表菲奥雷拉号两名幸存者的律师胡安·阿维拉 (Juan Avila) 告诉 Drop Site，被杀的检察官亚历山德拉·布拉沃 (Alexandra Bravo) 实际上是他的侄女。

sentences.en: The Coast Guard told Drop Site it “has no record of involvement with La Fiorella.”
sentences.zh: 海岸警卫队告诉 Drop Site，“没有与拉菲奥雷拉有牵连的记录”。

blocks.html_en: The absence of an assigned police detail when Bravo was murdered bears similarities to the 2023 assassination of frontrunner presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio. A congressional commission determined that Villavicencio’s police detail was insufficient, that he had been unconventionally escorted through an exposed street-level exit contrary to standard protocol, and that the armored vehicle designated to protect Villavicencio on the campaign trail had been left by his security team in another city that day. These breaches made him particularly vulnerable when assailants approached and shot him on the sidewalk as he was leaving a meeting with other government officials.

sentences.en: The absence of an assigned police detail when Bravo was murdered bears similarities to the 2023 assassination of frontrunner presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio.
sentences.zh: 布拉沃被谋杀时没有指派警察参与，这与 2023 年总统候选人费尔南多·比亚维森西奥 (Fernando Villavicencio) 遇刺事件有相似之处。

sentences.en: A congressional commission determined that Villavicencio’s police detail was insufficient, that he had been unconventionally escorted through an exposed street-level exit contrary to standard protocol, and that the armored vehicle designated to protect Villavicencio on the campaign trail had been left by his security team in another city that day.
sentences.zh: 国会委员会确定，比亚维森西奥的警察细节不足，他被非常规地护送通过一个暴露的街道出口，这违反了标准协议，而且指定在竞选途中保护比亚维森西奥的装甲车当天被他的安全团队留在了另一个城市。

sentences.en: These breaches made him particularly vulnerable when assailants approached and shot him on the sidewalk as he was leaving a meeting with other government officials.
sentences.zh: 当他离开与其他政府官员的会议时，袭击者在人行道上走近并向他开枪，这些违规行为使他特别容易受到伤害。

blocks.html_en: Villavicencio’s death cleared the way for now-President Daniel Noboa’s campaign—which had been polling at 3%—to surge to victory. 厄瓜多尔基多——负责调查美国袭击三艘厄瓜多尔船只以及 36 名幸存者随后遭受酷刑和绑架的叙述的检察官亚历山德拉·布拉沃 (Alexandra Bravo) 上个月在沿海城市曼塔被枪杀。 据警方称，6 月 14 日上午 11 点左右，当布拉沃和她的妹妹离开一家咖啡馆时，一名骑着黑色摩托车的杀手向布拉沃开枪。 布拉沃的妹妹跳下来保护她，也在袭击中丧生。

到达犯罪现场后，警方表示，他们发现了 5 个 9 毫米弹壳和布拉沃受伤的司机，但没有看到被指派保护她的警察人员的踪迹。 完全在行政部门领导下运作的警察局已启动调查，以确定是否存在内部安全漏洞。

布拉沃是厄瓜多尔司法系统自 2020 年以来第 26 名被暗杀的成员，也是本周第二名被谋杀的国家犯罪调查人员。 除了平常处理的凶杀案和有组织犯罪案件外，布拉沃还负责处理菲奥雷拉案、内格拉·弗朗西斯卡案和唐·马卡案——四月份 Drop Site 曝光的一系列针对民用渔船的无人机袭击事件。 两名船员回国后报告称，在一艘悬挂美国国旗的巡逻船上，被穿着美国军装的美国枪手绑架、蒙住眼睛并挨饿了八天，然后被遗弃在萨尔瓦多。 联合国强迫失踪委员会赞同开展调查的呼吁，要求美国在 4 月 27 日之前提供有关 8 名仍然失踪男子的下落以及是否参与此事的信息。 截至目前，美国尚未做出回应。

厄瓜多尔右翼总统丹尼尔·诺博亚（出生于迈阿密的亿万富翁，常被称为“美国支持的独裁者”）在厄瓜多尔的领导下，该国已成为“南方之矛”行动的中心试验场，这是华盛顿旨在针对“毒品恐怖分子”的法外轰炸行动，迄今为止已造成 221 人死亡。 没有证据表明许多受害者，包括布拉沃调查中的受害者，曾参与贩毒。

“我无法断言这是一次政治暗杀，但显然，一名检察官被杀是因为他们正在进行的调查，”厄瓜多尔 CDH 著名人权律师、总部位于日内瓦的世界反酷刑组织成员费尔南多·巴斯蒂亚斯 (Fernando Bastias) 告诉 Drop Site，“这是我们从厄瓜多尔的经历中学到的东西。”

曼塔警察局内部一位认识布拉沃的消息人士告诉 Drop Site，厄瓜多尔检察官受到总检察长办公室上级的压力，要求将美国袭击事件仅视为“失踪案件”。 该消息人士因担心遭到报复而要求匿名，他表示，44 名失踪男子中的 36 人被发现后，布拉沃被告知关闭所有调查线，尽管他们抵达时身受重伤，包括 70% 的视力丧失和双脚被撕碎，医学专家认为这与他们对爆炸和酷刑的描述相符。

人权观察组织的一位高级研究员在对三艘船只进行调查时采访了布拉沃，她同样回忆说，布拉沃面临“机构内部推进调查的内部挑战”。 研究人员表示，检察官多次寻求负责该船救援的其他部门的合作，包括曼塔港船长局，但“没有人回应她索取信息的请求”。 在内格拉·弗朗西斯卡爆炸期间，附近一艘船上的目击者达尔文·皮科·弗洛雷斯告诉 Drop Site，他致电曼塔港船长请求紧急援助。 没有人来。 今年四月，作为对该事件首次调查的一部分，Drop Site 致电该港口寻求评论。 官员们在得知电话是记者打来后挂断了电话。

研究人员告诉 Drop Site，截至 5 月 8 日的最后一次会议，Bravo“仍处于询问和调查的初始阶段”。 巴斯蒂亚斯表示，布拉沃“正在调查一个被媒体定位为打击犯罪盟友的国家（美国）。 这项调查根本没有进展，这是出于避免与任何人陷入麻烦或问题的意图。”

曼塔警察局内部消息人士称，鉴于合作机构缺乏合作，布拉沃已就如何寻找新的证据来源征求建议。

在她去世前几天，布拉沃被调往邻近城市蒙特克里斯蒂的总检察长办公室。 调职后，她的案件量发生了变化，她不再负责调查三起船只袭击事件。 Drop Site 试图联系布拉沃的继任者请其置评，但他被明确指示不要接受媒体采访。 经过数周的尝试联系总检察长办公室征求意见后，他们告诉 Drop Site，调查已经结束，他们无法就 Bravo 搬迁的原因发表评论。

在美国支持的厄瓜多尔军政权内部，总检察长办公室已成为一个日益不透明和政治化的机构。 “这已经成为检察官调查当地国家特工的主要障碍。 现在想象一下国际国家特工，”巴斯蒂亚斯说。 他补充说：“行政部门已经实施了一系列法律框架，使这些外国国家特工免受起诉。”他指的是诺博亚总统的 22 项戒严法令赋予所有美国军方和国防部人员的外交豁免权。

五角大楼、海岸警卫队和美国南方司令部均否认对船只事故知情或不承担任何责任。 在 Drop Site 发布了内格拉·弗朗西斯卡爆炸事件的照片证据后，美国议员在国会听证会上对美国战争部长皮特·赫格斯提出了质询。 6 月 13 日，即布拉沃被谋杀的前一天，众议员。 华金·卡斯特罗（德克萨斯州民主党）和比尔·基廷（马萨诸塞州民主党） 向赫格斯、国务卿马可·卢比奥和美国海岸警卫队负责人凯文·伦迪发表了一封信，要求对美国政府参与袭击事​​件进行全面审计。 尽管截止日期为 7 月 10 日，但尚未有任何机构发表公开回应。 基廷的新闻秘书劳伦·麦克德莫特告诉 Drop Site，他的办公室已收到卢比奥办公室的回复，但没有收到来自战争部或海岸警卫队的回复。 她没有透露回应的内容。

返回家园的幸存者以及没有回家的幸存者的家人仍然没有收到任何答复，他们告诉 Drop Site“当局当着我们的面关上了门。” 其中一名渔民的妻子玛丽亚告诉 Drop Site，她的婆婆在等待儿子回来时去世，她说她一直在与严重的抑郁症作斗争，在去世前几周就停止了抑郁。

尽管两国政府都努力阻挠调查，但不断有证据支持渔民关于绑架、空袭和酷刑的说法。 Drop Site 获得了美国海岸警卫队在 Negra Francisca 爆炸案附近活动的独家视频、证实 Negra Francisca 证词的开源情报，以及警方对目击者的采访，证实了幸存者声称的、由 Drop Site 记录的美国参与其中的情况。 在 Airwars OSINT 分析师和前美国海军陆战队成员托米·麦克拉斯基 (Tomi McCluskey) 的帮助下，Drop Site 获取了更多 NASA 热图像，这些图像与内格拉·弗朗西斯卡 (Negra Francisca) 爆炸事件一致，以及船只跟踪数据，显示美国海岸警卫队活动沿渔民所说的袭击后拍摄的路线进行。

Drop Site 获得的视频显示，据称海岸警卫队在 Negra Francisca 罢工附近活动。

通过军事宵禁和政治犯大规模饥饿进行统治的诺博亚竭尽全力成为特朗普在南美洲最强大的合作伙伴。 自上任以来，他无视厄瓜多尔宪法禁止美国驻军的规定——截至 2025 年 11 月，该禁令已获得 60% 的选民批准——该禁令最初于近 20 年前出台，正是因为美国军队在曼塔海岸击沉船只的历史。 此外，他的政府授权在厄瓜多尔领土上设立第一个联邦调查局办事处，协助美国大使馆在选举前诬陷哥伦比亚左翼政府成员，并与美国合作轰炸哥伦比亚和厄瓜多尔边境的无辜平民农场工人——所有这些都是以打击贩毒的名义。

值得注意的是，诺博亚家族航运公司的船只因贩运价值 2600 万英镑的可卡因而被抓获——这一细节并没有阻止国务院任命他为特朗普反毒战争的关键合作伙伴。 上个月，《卫报》报道称，一名正在调查诺博亚与贩毒关系的举报人被谋杀。

尽管如此，诺博亚仍然是特朗普美洲之盾中信誉良好的成员。 美洲反卡特尔联盟也被称为“盾牌”，它既是一个军事联盟，也是一个高度政治的联盟，在总统罗德里戈·帕斯面对反紧缩抗议活动时，该联盟公开干预以支持美国在玻利维亚的利益。

当地检察官指控美军对厄瓜多尔平民进行法外爆炸和酷刑，这将破坏两国联盟并损害厄瓜多尔与美国的关系。关系。

其他调查美国与厄瓜多尔犯罪勾结的政府官员也收到了死亡威胁。 代表居住在美国的厄瓜多尔人的国民议会议员莫妮卡·帕拉西奥斯(Mónica Palacios)宣布计划将菲奥雷拉船案提交联合国，在揭露美国-厄瓜多尔政府贪污丑闻后，她面临数月的政治法律诉讼。 上周五，帕拉西奥斯表示，她收到了针对自己和一岁儿子的死亡威胁，以及她纽约家外面的录像。 她直接指责诺博亚总统，称这些威胁是对她对美国-厄瓜多尔腐败调查的报复。

人权律师巴斯蒂亚斯表示：“法官和检察官受到直接迫害，他们在职责范围内做出的决定与行政部门的要求不完全一致，最终受到制裁。” “另一方面，也存在犯罪背景带来的风险。” 他断言，无论如何，布拉沃的死亡“与国家做什么或不做什么有很大关系，因为到目前为止，司法系统公务员还没有任何有效的安全机制。 责任在于未能确保保护。”

厄瓜多尔国民议会前议员、现任厄瓜多尔共产党发言人迭戈·文蒂米拉·贾林 (Diego Vintimilla Jarrín) 同样告诉 Drop Site，“诺博亚政府是我们自民主开始以来最反主权的政府。 我没有证据证明是谁谋杀了检察官，但事实上她正在调查某些因素，而这些因素后来似乎不再重要，这一事实也说明了很多根本问题。”

美国坚称其从未与这三艘船中的任何一艘进行过互动。 美国海岸警卫队发言人告诉《卫报》，该机构参与这些事件的唯一原因是在收到“内格拉·弗朗西斯卡号”起火的“MAYDAY”警报后，部署 USCGC Bertholf 号执行搜救任务，但最终什么也没发现。

但麦克拉斯基专门向空投站提供的伯索夫号行动追踪数据显示，轰炸机在爆炸发生前后就位于内格拉·弗朗西斯号附近，随后关闭了信号——结果在同一天内格拉·弗朗西斯卡号船员被带入中美洲水域并被转移到萨尔瓦多海军司令部的同一天再次出现在哥斯达黎加海岸附近，他们的四肢在袭击中被严重烧伤。 “内格拉·弗朗西斯卡”号船长埃尔南·弗洛雷斯 (Hernán Flores) 告诉 Drop Site，萨尔瓦多官员特别通知他，“美国人员已致电协调交接事宜。”

海岸警卫队否认其协调过交接工作。 一位发言人表示：“海岸警卫队在从内格拉弗朗西斯卡杜阿尔特二世号转移渔民的过程中没有发挥任何作用。”

USCGC Bertholf 于下午 4 点离开加拉帕戈斯军事基地。 3 月 16 日，不久之后就停止传输其位置。 一天后，内格拉弗朗西斯卡号在 170 英里外遭到轰炸——通常乘船需要 3 到 10 小时才能到达这个距离。 空投点要求美国海岸警卫队对快艇信号消失后的活动进行解释。 海岸警卫队回应称，“出于行动安全考虑，不会披露执法任务期间的巡逻艇动向”。

下午 1:02 3 月 17 日，NASA FIRMS 记录到了与爆炸性火灾一致的热异常现象，证实了 Negra Francisca 渔民告诉 Drop Site 他们的船被多架无人机袭击起火的时间和地点。 机组人员表示，他们随后被身穿卡其布迷彩服、袖子上缝有美国国旗补丁的金发英语男子用枪指着——他们的描述与美国南方司令部新闻稿中的制服相符。 据称，在这艘悬挂美国国旗的巡逻船上，枪手将他们扣为人质，击沉了被炸毁的船只，用头罩蒙住他们的头，殴打了一些渔民，并在将他们运往中美洲的过程中扣留了八天的食物。

3 月 22 日，USCGC Bertholf 的信号在戈尔菲托港附近的哥斯达黎加水域重新出现，距离萨尔瓦多水域约 450 海里。 它关闭了应答器，直到 3 月 24 日才重新启动，即萨尔瓦多海岸警卫队公开宣布拘留 Negra Francisca 渔民 24 小时后。

作为我们首次调查的一部分，Drop Site 联系了萨尔瓦多的 11 名政府人员。 他们都以媒体禁言令为由拒绝公开记录。

伯索夫号曾有先例将美国空袭的受害者转移给中美洲当局，哥斯达黎加媒体报道称，该船大约在同一时间将两名死者和一名受伤幸存者的遗体运送到哥斯达黎加的戈尔菲托港。 哥斯达黎加海事检查员威尔伯·乌罗兹·吉多(Wilber Urroz Guido)表示，他不知道这艘快艇的动向，但它被授权根据美国和哥斯达黎加之间的谅解备忘录采取行动，类似于美国与厄瓜多尔和萨尔瓦多维持的协议。

目击者的证词也让人对美国海岸警卫队对事件的描述产生怀疑。 袭击事件目击者、内格拉·弗朗西斯卡船长的侄子达尔文·弗洛雷斯-皮科 (Darwin Flores-Pico) 与 Drop Site 独家分享的视频片段显示，一艘美国海岸警卫队快艇正在爆炸发生的水域巡逻。

Drop Site 获得的视频显示，据称海岸警卫队在 Negra Francisca 罢工附近活动。

达尔文说，3 月 17 日，他在附近的 Solavil 号船上钓鱼，下午 2 点左右，他发现远处升起浓烟。 当他多次尝试通过无线电联系内格拉·弗朗西斯卡号的机组人员时，他发现一架美国飞机在上空盘旋。 直到几个小时后，他才通过无线电信号得知“内格拉·弗朗西斯卡”号起火了，于是他赶到现场，发现船只已被大火吞噬，没有幸存者的迹象。

他找到了两艘烧焦的应急船，拍下了火灾的照片证据，然后致电曼塔港寻求帮助。 没有人来。

达尔文决定开始返回港口寻求紧急援助，当他离开火灾现场时，红色和绿色的灯光落在了内格拉·弗朗西斯卡号上。 由于担心自己的安全，他将船驶离了现场。

第二天下午，达尔文告诉 Drop Site，他的船被美国海岸警卫队登上，美国海岸警卫队通过带有波多黎各口音的西班牙语翻译拘留并审问了船员近 12 个小时。 他说，海岸警卫队人员确认红灯和绿灯来自他们的巡逻队，并承认前一天晚上到达了内格拉·弗朗西斯卡号的现场，但拒绝详细说明他们发现的任何内容。

相反，他们询问渔民是否看到任何东西以及达尔文为何打捞小船。 达尔文说，在告诉海岸警卫队官员内格拉·弗朗西斯卡号是他叔叔的船后，他们突然停止询问他，并开始用英语通过无线电与视频中显示的附近快艇上的同事进行交流。 达尔文说：“由于我们是唯一看到一切的人，我们担心他们可能会对我们做点什么。” 他觉得美国海岸警卫队对帮助他找到家人没有兴趣，而是似乎更专注于“确保我们不是任何事情的目击者”。

麦克拉斯基说，三艘船所描述的多无人机战术反映了美国的原则。 他认为，从邻国到有组织犯罪集团的其他地区大国不太可能有预算或获得此类技术。 尽管海岸警卫队也否认在厄瓜多尔水域使用武装无人机，但卡特尔在海域深处使用“天眼”监视无人机尚无先例。

此外，让幸存者活着的决定，尽管涉及酷刑证词，以及运送他们的努力和费用，比任何有组织犯罪集团通常愿意采取的做法更能反映国防部的协议——旨在避免国际法律后果。 “如果是卡特尔，你永远找不到他们，”麦克拉斯基说。 “不会有幸存者可以交谈，不会有故事。”

“菲奥雷拉”号于 1 月 20 日在加拉帕戈斯群岛海岸被击中；船上八名渔民全部失踪。 船只消失的前一天，船长的妻子接到丈夫打来的紧急电话，警告美国飞机正在上空盘旋。

Drop Site 从两名目击者克里斯蒂安·弗洛雷斯 (Christian Flores) 和迪马斯·伊格纳西奥·阿尔瓦雷斯 (Dimas Ignacio Álvarez) 那里获得了警方的采访笔录，他们证实看到菲奥雷拉号被烟雾吞没，并被美国资产包围。 这两名男子是“菲奥雷拉”号船员，但在附近的一艘木筏上拉长绳几个小时后，船只冒烟了。

弗洛雷斯和阿尔瓦雷斯在警方声明中描述了 1 月 18 日两架美国飞机飞越菲奥雷拉上空的情况； 1月19日，多架灰色美国无人机和一艘悬挂美国国旗的巡逻舰在该船周围盘旋； 1 月 20 日——他们的船员失踪的那一天——一艘悬挂美国国旗的大型巡逻船在烟雾附近。 从远处看，他们无法辨认船上的人员，但他们的说法与“内格拉·弗朗西斯卡”号船员的说法相呼应，他们说，他们在一艘悬挂美国国旗的巡逻船上被武装的美国人扣为人质。 目击者的描述也与美国南方司令部公开帖子中介绍的飞机和设备相符。

发现烟雾后，两名渔民表示，他们听到船员通过无线电向船长求救。 他们再也没有被见过。

代表菲奥雷拉号两名幸存者的律师胡安·阿维拉 (Juan Avila) 告诉 Drop Site，被杀的检察官亚历山德拉·布拉沃 (Alexandra Bravo) 实际上是他的侄女。

海岸警卫队告诉 Drop Site，“没有与拉菲奥雷拉有牵连的记录”。

布拉沃被谋杀时没有指派警察参与，这与 2023 年总统候选人费尔南多·比亚维森西奥 (Fernando Villavicencio) 遇刺事件有相似之处。 国会委员会确定，比亚维森西奥的警察细节不足，他被非常规地护送通过一个暴露的街道出口，这违反了标准协议，而且指定在竞选途中保护比亚维森西奥的装甲车当天被他的安全团队留在了另一个城市。 当他离开与其他政府官员的会议时，袭击者在人行道上走近并向他开枪，这些违规行为使他特别容易受到伤害。

比亚维森西奥的去世为现任总统丹尼尔·诺博亚（Daniel Noboa）的竞选活动（民意调查率为 3%）大获胜利扫清了道路。 国民议会议员、比亚维森西奥党派成员吉塞拉·莫利纳（Gisella Molina）在刺杀事件中与他在一起并受伤，在接受《Señal Columbia》采访时表示，政府官员事先了解这一阴谋。

在 2024 年谋杀案调查期间，Drop Site 发布了时任司法部长戴安娜·萨拉查 (Diana Salazar) 的私人信息，揭露了在与美国大使密切合作的情况下将前民主社会主义总统科雷亚 (Correa) 的政党牵涉到比亚维森西奥 (Villavicencio) 暗杀事件的阴谋。

该州后来得出结论，洛斯洛博斯贩毒集团实施了比亚维森西奥谋杀案，并声称科雷亚政党的前成员是主谋。 检察官声称，洛斯·洛博斯因揭露其犯罪网络而杀害了比亚维森西奥。 尽管比亚维森西奥致力于根除卡特尔经济，但诺博亚领导下的厄瓜多尔（被指控为有组织犯罪头目提供豁免权以换取选举支持）已成为全球 70% 可卡因的最大分销中心。

布拉沃死后，司法部长立即发表公开声明，将她的谋杀归咎于对打击有组织犯罪的检察官的报复。 当被问及为什么当局将这起杀戮与有组织犯罪联系起来以及调查人员是否发现了有关布拉沃失踪的警察保护细节的任何信息时，总检察长办公室告诉 Drop Site 调查正在进行中，并拒绝发表评论。

尽管总检察长尚未提供证据支持他们的主张，布拉沃向人权观察表示遗憾，称她的工作中“危险始终存在”。 “她说，在有组织犯罪的背景下担任检察官既复杂又危险，但她没有提供任何进一步的细节，”研究人员告诉 Drop Site。 曼塔位于厄瓜多尔有组织犯罪危机的中心，这个南美国家成为西半球最暴力的国家。

Bravo 还负责调查 2024 年 Patricia Lynn 轮船及其 21 名船员失踪的悬而未决的案件。

布拉沃是与帕特里夏·林恩案有关的第二个被暗杀的人。 第一个是一名失踪渔民的婆婆，她成为受害者家属的发言人，并组织游行，要求为失踪亲人提供答案。 玛丽亚·乔兹 (María Chóez) 在曼塔市中心经营街头小吃摊时被两名武装袭击者开枪打死。

人权观察研究员表示，帕特里夏·林恩号船只在厄瓜多尔水域沉没，“成为所有这些与船只有关的事件的先例”。

“如果厄瓜多尔对其机构有一个信任框架，人们可能会认为[布拉沃被谋杀]是一起普通犯罪，”前议员文蒂米拉·贾林(Vintimilla Jarrin)说。 “但考虑到针对法官、检察官和律师的系统性暴力行为，没有太多空间让他们从无罪推定。 二十六名司法系统成员被谋杀是一个令人震惊的数字。 当然，整个危机是由政府当局直接推动的议程引发的。从有组织犯罪中受益的是大权力集团。”
